How reaching out works — a gentle map

A short, transparent outline so you know what to expect.
1
Initial contact
Use the form, call, or email. I’ll reply with intake details and available times within 48 business hours.
2
First conversation
A 20–30 minute brief call or intake session to clarify needs, confidentiality, and fit. Together we decide next steps.
3
Ongoing sessions
Regularly scheduled sessions, collaboratively set goals, and periodic check-ins about care and boundaries.

What people often tell me helps

• Practical tools for anxiety and panic that fit daily life.
• Space to process past experiences without pressure or judgement.
• Relational patterns explored with curiosity and respect.

Testimonials

“Working with {{THERAPIST_NAME}} helped me feel seen and steady. The pacing was thoughtful and practical.” — A client in {{CITY}}
Client names are withheld. Testimonials are shared with permission and represent individual experiences, not guaranteed outcomes.

Quick contact

Sessions are confidential within the limits of the law. For emergencies or if you are in crisis, please call local emergency services or the national crisis line. I do not provide emergency services.

Send a private message

Or email directly
By sending this form you agree to receive a reply by email or phone. I will protect your information; see privacy notes below.

FAQ — About contacting and beginning therapy

Will you answer a question about my insurance?
I can provide general information about fees and typical session length. For exact benefits, please check directly with your insurer. I may provide a superbill on request.
How quickly will I hear back?
I aim to respond to contact requests within 48 business hours. If you do not hear back, please try the phone number above.
Do you work with couples or families?
I primarily offer individual therapy; limited couples work may be available by arrangement. We can discuss fit during the brief intake conversation.
Notes on scope, privacy, and safety:
  • Confidentiality: Communications with me are confidential except where required by law (e.g., imminent risk of harm to self or others, or suspected abuse of a minor/elder). Please avoid sharing highly sensitive details via unsecured email or public devices.
  • Not an emergency service: If you are in immediate danger, call emergency services or your local crisis line. If you are in the U.S., the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is available at 988.
  • Limits of care: Therapy involves exploring difficult emotions and memories; progress varies and cannot be guaranteed. We will collaborate on goals and review treatment plans regularly.

SVGs referenced in the wider project are local (assets/img/hero.svg, avatar.svg, pattern.svg) — ensure those are provided in the completed bundle. - The contact form uses a simple POST to {{PRIMARY_CTA_URL}}. If you prefer mailto behavior or integration with a serverless endpoint, swap the form action accordingly. Accessibility & privacy: - Labels are associated with inputs. - Short content for testimonials and process to reduce cognitive load. - Clear crisis disclaimer and confidentiality limits are included. Do not remove these — they are essential for ethical presentation. How to preview locally: - Place this file alongside the other site HTML files in a folder and open contact.html in a browser. - For production, replace the placeholders with real values (or a template engine of your choice) and ensure the form action points to a real intake endpoint. Customization notes: - Colors and radii are set in :root for easy adjustment. - The CTA and the Welcome Guide link both use {{PRIMARY_CTA_URL}} for convenience; you can point the Guide to a direct file (e.g., /assets/welcome-guide.pdf) if you host it locally. Ethical reminder: - The language avoids medical claims and frames therapy as supportive. Keep copy consistent with local licensing rules and professional guidelines."} BUNDLE_END
